Beállítom Magyar Péter miniszterelnök a Mavir, azaz a Magyar Villamosenergia-ipari Átviteli Rendszerirányító Zrt. vezénylő központjából jelentkezett be hétfő este, a Védelmi Munkacsoport ülése után. A kormányfő azt mondta a Facebookon közzétett videójában , hogy országosan figyelik az energiafogyasztás egyensúlyát, „jelenleg már jócskán benne járunk a legkritikusabb időszakban”. Magyar a vezénylő központban lévő térképen megmutatta, hogy jelenleg a hálózat terhelése 6300 megawatt környékén jár. „Az áramfogyasztás ma is, ahogy az elmúlt napokban is, jóval lejjebb jár a tervezettnél” – mondta, hozzátéve, hogy az eltérés meghaladja az 500 megawattot. Ennyivel fogyaszt kevesebbet az ország a szakértői előrejelzésekhez képest. A miniszterelnök azt reméli, hogy a nap kritikus óráiban és a következő napokban is fenn tudják tartani ezt az előnyt. „Ha ezt el tudjuk érni, akkor továbbra is igaz lesz, hogy nem szükséges szigorúbb beavatkozás” – fogalmazott. Magyar Péter a nagyfogyasztó vállalatokról azt mondta, hogy a hétfői adatok szerint összesen már több mint 630 megawattnyi önkéntes korlátozást vállaltak. De továbbra is elvárják az önkéntes hozzájárulást, és ha lehetséges, vállaljanak a korábbinál nagyobb teljesítménycsökkentést. Magyar egy vállalatot név szerint is megemlített, a Mészáros Lőrinc érdekeltségébe tartozó izocukorgyárat, a Kall Ingredients Kft.-t, a vállalat eddig ugyanis nem válaszolt arra, hogy vállalja-e a 13 megawattos fogyasztásuk önkéntes visszafogását. „Innen is üzenem az olasz partoknál ringatózó, Rose d'Or nevű harmincmilliárdos jacht tulajdonosának, hogy még nem késő önkéntes felajánlást tenni, ahogy azt megtette több száz másik vállalat is” – mondta a miniszterelnök, utalva arra a luxusjachtra , amin 2023 óta többször is lefotózták Mészáros Lőrincet és a feleségét. A paksi vízállásról azt mondta Magyar, hogy jelenleg stagnál a vízszint, és a következő órákban eldőlhet, hogy megőrizhető-e a termelés az utolsó paksi turbinánál. Szerinte biztató jel, hogy Budapesten megállt a Duna apadása, sőt, egy centiméterrel emelkedett a vízszint. Hozzátette, hogy folyamatosan kapcsolatban van a paksi atomerőmű vezetésével. Arról, hogy milyen durva stresszteszt lehet, ha tényleg leállítják a paksi atomerőművet, ebben a cikkünkben írtunk részletesen . Magyar közölte: a szerda lehet a legnehezebb nap, „amikor a hőség már olyan mértékben melegíti fel az épületeket és az aszfaltot, hogy az az energiafogyasztásban is meglátszódhat”. A miniszterelnök felszólította a vállalatokat, hogy egész héten tartsák be a 17 és 22 óra közötti önkéntes fogyasztáscsökkentésüket, és a lakosságot is arra kérte, hogy ebben az időszakban figyeljenek az áramfogyasztásukra. US News Authorities Arrest Fugitive Behind Alleged $547 Million Medicare Fraud The person is the third individual on the Most Wanted Fraudsters list to be captured in the past five weeks, the FBI director said. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print Khalid Satary’s arrival at Washington Dulles International Airport. Courtesy of the DOJ Naveen Athrappully Reporter 7/23/2026 | Updated: 7/23/2026 0:00 X 1 A man on the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters list, accused of a scheme to defraud Medicare of $547 million, was arrested by authorities on Monday. The foreign national, Khalid Satary, 54, owned and operated multiple diagnostic testing laboratories in the United States between 2016 and 2019 that billed Medicare for “expensive and medically unnecessary genetic tests,” the Department of Justice (DOJ) said in a July 21 statement. Satary is accused of conspiring with several patient recruiters and telemarketing services to generate unnecessary cancer genetic test samples that were reimbursed by Medicare at the rate of $10,000 to $20,000 per sample. To run the operation, Satary allegedly paid millions of dollars in bribes and illegal kickbacks to patient recruiters and doctors. The defendant was initially indicted in 2019. However, Satary was later released on bond, with the condition that he doesn’t work in the healthcare sector. While on bond, Satary allegedly conspired with labs in Texas to continue submitting fraudulent genetic testing claims to Medicare. A federal arrest warrant was issued against him in December 2022. However, Satary failed to appear for a court hearing and was believed to have escaped the United States. On July 20 this year, the defendant was arrested in the Middle East with a fake Mexican passport using a fake name. He was then transferred to U.S. authorities. Related Stories Lawmakers Propose $28 Billion Investment to Combat Fraud Groups Sue for Communication Records Linked to Somali Daycare Fraud Claims The Most Wanted Fraudsters list was announced by FBI Director Kash Patel last month. The White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud partnered with the FBI to compile the list, according to a June 19 X post from Vice President JD Vance, the task force’s chairman. The task force was established through a March 16 executive order signed by President Donald Trump, which said criminals and other individuals were exploiting various benefit programs intended to provide American citizens with a safety net. Trump ordered the task force to “coordinate and accelerate a comprehensive national strategy to stop fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.” One of those on the list, Said Abdullahi Ereg, surrendered to law enforcement on June 10, according to the FBI and federal prosecutors. Ereg is accused of laundering millions of dollars from a program that aimed to feed needy children during the COVID-19 pandemic. Another individual on the list, Herbert Leon Kimble, accused of $1.2 billion Medicare fraud, was arrested on June 11 in the Philippines. In its latest statement, the DOJ said that Satary has been charged with various fraud-related crimes, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and paying bribes and illegal healthcare kickbacks. He faces a multi-decade prison term if convicted. “The arrest of Khalid Ahmed Satary and return to the U.S. is the third Most Wanted Fraudster capture from this FBI and our partners in just five weeks—continuing the historic run of success for this new initiative,” Patel said in the statement. “This is another subject who exploited a program dedicated to helping our most vulnerable and instead stole for himself. Satary has been on the run since 2022, but we got him thanks to great work and coordination from the interagency and our overseas partners.” The Epoch Times was unable to reach Satary’s legal representative. According to the FBI’s website, Satary is one among nine individuals currently mentioned on the Most Wanted Fraudsters list. One of the individuals is a naturalized U.S. citizen of Somali origin wanted for allegedly being part of a fraud scheme that exploited the federal Child Nutrition Program during the COVID-19 pandemic. Another individual, a female from Jamaica, is linked to a scheme that fraudulently obtained more than $32 million from COVID-19 relief funds. A third person, a U.S. citizen, is wanted for alleged involvement in a mail fraud scheme in Georgia. The man allegedly defrauded at least $10 million from his victims. Meanwhile, on June 23, the DOJ announced that a coordinated enforcement action involving a whole-of-government approach led to the arrests of 455 individuals for their alleged role in healthcare fraud and opioid abuse schemes. The schemes, which involved more than $6.5 billion in false claims, posed “significant patient harm,” including death. Among the arrested were two Estonians connected to a $10.6 billion fraud scheme. Photograph: James Petermeier/Zuma Press/Shutterstock Netherlands Dutch riot police break up violent far-right protest in The Hague Authorities ban anti-immigration march after fireworks and other projectiles thrown at officers in city centre park Associated Press in The Hague Sat 19 Sep 2026 15.43 EDT First published on Sat 19 Sep 2026 13.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred far-right protesters in The Hague on Saturday after violence erupted and local authorities banned a planned march in the city against immigration and asylum policies. The Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported that 24 people had been arrested, after some protesters threw fireworks and other projectiles at police. Justice minister David van Weel called on X for an “extremely firm” response to what he described as “disgusting scenes” at the protest, organised by the far-right We Are the People organisation. He said demonstrators made Nazi salutes, chanted antisemitic slogans, and attacked and threw fireworks at police. “Thanks to all the police officers who are once again standing up for our democratic rule of law,” he wrote. View image in fullscreen The march was organised to protest about immigration and asylum policies in the Netherlands. Photograph: James Petermeier/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock The Hague municipality banned the march after violence broke out among demonstrators gathered at the Malieveld, a park in the city centre, and later ordered the crowd to disperse. Those arrested were detained for various offences, including failing to comply with the order and illegally possessing weapons. Police reportedly used pepper spray and a water cannon on the rioters. Saturday’s unrest came a year after rioting erupted during a rightwing demonstration in The Hague. A police car was set on fire during the clashes between black-clad protesters and police. The headquarters of the centrist D66 party – whose leader, Rob Jetten, is now prime minister – was also attacked. Jetten said on X that the demonstrators deliberately sought confrontation with the police and chanted “abhorrent” far-right and antisemitic slogans.
